strengths: Well-motivated research question challenging the 'depth = safety' intuition in collaborative inference partitioning
Solid information-theoretic framework with rigorous proofs deriving H(X|Z) lower bounds for feature vs. decision-level representations
Comprehensive experimental validation across four representative architectures (IR-152, ResNet-50, VGG19, ViT) and multiple datasets with consistent findings
Novel analysis of label smoothing effects on representation geometry and R²_c evolution with clear gradient-based derivations
Practical algorithm (Algorithm 1) for automatic Golden Partition Zone localization that is easy to implement
Thorough deployment cost analysis (Appendix I) providing actionable guidance for practitioners on privacy-utility-latency tradeoffs
Excellent experimental design with stress-testing via enhanced inversion models and intermediate information enrichment (Tables 3-4)
Detailed supplementary material including proofs, ablations, and implementation details supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited experimental scope: all images at 64×64 resolution with no evaluation on high-resolution data, language models, or other modalities beyond vision

Theoretical bounds contain loose finite-precision correction terms (κ_Δ) and rely on Gaussian assumptions not empirically validated; gap between bound and empirical 'abrupt' increase not fully explained

Architecture-dependent results significantly limit generalizability: ViT shows no clear GPZ, ResNet delays transition requiring 78% edge-side parameters, suggesting phenomenon is architecture-specific rather than universal principle
Inversion models based on relatively standard architectures; state-of-the-art generative approaches (diffusion-based) less thoroughly evaluated, potentially affecting resistance estimates
Neural Vortex concept explicitly acknowledged as metaphorical rather than a formal mechanism, somewhat weakening novelty of the conceptual contribution
No head-to-head comparison with existing CI defenses (Wang et al., 2022; Xia et al., 2025); authors justify as characterization work, but benchmarking would strengthen claims
Causal relationship between R²_c and MIA resistance is indirect (through bounds on H(X|Z)); R²_c is a consequence of training dynamics rather than direct proxy for privacy
Auxiliary data quality is critical for attack success; strong assumption that attackers have high-quality distribution-matched data may not always hold in practice
